newsitem.title: IRAN: OPEC ministers schedule Iran talks for Thursday.
newsitem.headline: OPEC ministers schedule Iran talks for Thursday.

text.p: Seven OPEC oil ministers scheduled a meeting for Thursday evening here as concerns rise in the eleven-member oil producing group that quota busting is getting out of hand and damaging crude prices, OPEC sources said on Wednesday.
"There is a lot of oil in the market place both from us and from non-OPEC so some form of moderation is required," OPEC Secretary-General Rilwanu Lukman told Reuters.
Nigerian oil minister Dan Etete said an agenda for the discussions would be set on Thursday morning when OPEC's quota compliance committee resumes after a lengthy session on Wednesday.

"There is no precise agenda yet but you can be sure they will be looking at why prices came down so sharply this year," said an OPEC delegate. "Whether there is the will to do anything about it is another question."
International benchmark Brent blend crude was trading at $18.18 a barrel on Wednesday, down nearly seven dollars from early January.
Quota compliance committee talks chaired by Iran's Gholamreza Aghazadeh, were joined on Wednesday afternoon by Venezuelan oil minister Erwin Arrieta.

Venezuela, not a current member of the committee, is widely tagged as OPEC's biggest quota buster, pumping crude at some 3.18 million barrels per day (bpd) in March compared to its 2.359 million allocation.
Arrieta has consistently denied the charge despite the wealth of evidence to support it. He declined any comment on Wednesday.
Aghazadeh, one of OPEC's toughest price hawks, met Arrieta in private in Tehran earlier this week.
Current OPEC president Libya's Abdullah Salem al-Badri, Lukman and Etete also attended Wednesday's compliance session.

Al-Badri last month made an appeal to his OPEC colleagues to exercise some production restraint but apparently without success. OPEC production is estimated running almost two million bpd in excess of the official 25.03 million bpd ceiling.
Thursday's talks are expected to include Kuwait's Isa al-Mazeedi, Qatar's Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah and probably Indonesia's Ida Bagus Sudjana. OPEC kingpin Saudi Arabia will not be represented.
The discussions are likely to take place after the opening session of an industry conference being organised by the National Iranian Oil Corp. The session ends at 2100 local time (1600 GMT).
OPEC'S next full conference will be held in Vienna in June.
